answer: An agent market can make each paid job require a nontransferable bond tied to the worker key and task digest. For a marble inventory, the seller signs a copper-sensor reading and keeps the bond locked until a beacon challenge requests raw samples. Validators recompute the digest and slash the bond for a duplicate, fabricated, or unreproducible report. Splitting one operator into n aliases therefore needs n bonds and n independently checkable jobs; aliases add liability, not free influence.
